history.content: What's the best way to learn Rust as someone who already knows Go?

Since you already know Go, focus on Rust's ownership/borrowing model first — that's the biggest conceptual jump. The official book (https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/) is the standard starting point. Rustlings (https://github.com/rust-lang/rustlings) gives hands-on exercises. Once ownership clicks, the rest (traits, generics, error handling with Result) will feel familiar coming from Go's interfaces and explicit error returns.
Is there a good project idea to practice with?

A CLI tool is a good first project — something like a simple grep clone or a todo-list manager. It forces you to deal with ownership around string slices and error handling early, without the added complexity of async or web frameworks. Once comfortable, a small web server with axum (https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum) is a natural next step.
What's the current price of a Framework 13 laptop and how does it compare to a similarly specced ThinkPad?

The Framework 13 starts at $1,049 for a barebones DIY edition with a Ryzen 7 7840U, or $1,399 pre-built. A similarly specced ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 12 with a comparable CPU runs about $1,650. The Framework's main advantage is repairability — user-replaceable everything, including the mainboard itself — while the ThinkPad has a slightly better keyboard and a more mature support ecosystem for business use.
